scores.reason: Addresses momentum mechanism (candidate area) but no evidence of testing on small convnets, short training, or large batch; no concrete settings or effect sizes reported.
Analyzes Muon theoretically but identifies failure modes, not improvements; doesn't address sample-efficiency gains in practical regimes.
Newton-Schulz applied to Hidden Quantum Markov Models, not convnet optimization.
Orthogonalized momentum in federated setting with client-sampling noise; no supervised-learning or convnet experiments evident.

Directly proposes NAMO (adaptive Muon variant, candidate in question); claims negligible per-step overhead. Abstraction doesn't confirm experiments on small convnets, ≤10 epochs, or large batch. If full paper includes CIFAR-scale ablations, score would be 3.
Heavy-Ball momentum for diffusion model sampling, not supervised convnet training.
Muon with differential privacy; DP overhead worsens per-step cost and doesn't improve sample efficiency without external privacy constraint.
